newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: El Nino seen causing dry weather in east Australia.
newsitem.headline: El Nino seen causing dry weather in east Australia.

text.p: There is a strong possibility of significantly drier than normal weather expanding across much of eastern Australia in the coming months due to the effects of the El Nino phenomenon, Australia's Bureau of Meteorology said on Wednesday.
The El Nino continued to strengthen during June, it said.
"The central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean became warmer and the trade winds across most of the tropical Pacific are much weaker than normal," the bureau said.
Also, the Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) remained strongly negative, it said in its latest seasonal climate outlook.
Such data indicates the El Nino is the strongest since 1982/83, which was a period of severe drought in Australia, the bureau said.
Areas most at risk include most of Queensland and Victoria, southern New South Wales, southern South Australia and Tasmania, it said.
The outlook was based on a statistical system using a combination of rainfall patterns and trends in the SOI, a measure of the cross-Pacific atmospheric pressure gradient, the bureau said.
June rainfall across much of southern Australia was significantly below average, consistent with the near-extreme low value of the SOI and other strong El Nino characteristics, the bureau said.
Also, total rainfall since March has reflected the developing El Nino pattern, with significantly below average rainfall over South Australia, Victoria and parts of New South Wales, it said.
The bureau said it expects to next issue an update on the El Nino effect on August 5.

Prospects of drier than normal conditions meant Australian crop yields were more likely to be below average, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said earlier on Wednesday.
